correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the formal Euler-product reduction H-C=E(q)^(-1)[E(q)^(p^(2a))-E(q^(p^a))^(p^a)] in Z[[q]] and proved V/W=1+pZ implies V^(p^k)=W^(p^k) mod p^(k+1), also for p=2. At scale 0<=j<a, Frobenius and repeated p-power lifting force every coefficient before q^(p^j) to vanish modulo p^(2a-j+1), and the coefficient at q^(p^j) to equal -p^(2a-j) modulo that modulus. Since E(q)^(-1) is an integral unit of constant term one, it preserves the first nonzero coefficient index. The r<=a+1 and r>=2a+1 endpoints agree, including a=1. Independent bounded Euler-factor expansions for p=2,3,5 and several a verified the claimed first failures; these do not prove the infinitely quantified formula.

originality.rationale: Sharma arXiv:2610.01422v1 proves a comparison modulo p^a for t=p^a and the stronger prime case modulo p^2; its different first-failure analysis concerns t with nontrivial coprime factor. Han develops the generating-function formula and Han–Ono compares zero sets at t=3. None of their inspected results states or implies the full p-adic first discrepancy staircase for arbitrary a. A standard higher-order Frobenius lifting corollary or older eta-product congruence remains a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: The exact maximal uniform prime-power congruence p^(a+1), sharp leading residues, and every first failure index d_{p,a}(r) give a complete natural filtration invariant of two established partition generating functions. They answer an explicitly motivated higher-lifting question beyond a single numerical congruence; the unrestricted arithmetic law is not a mere parameter renaming or a known finite table.

limitations: Only t=p^a; not all coefficient valuations for each index or mixed-prime t.
Checks for finite p,a only corroborate the infinite proof.
